title: Audi’s new A2 E-tron is its most affordable and efficient EV yet
summary: Audi's new A2 E-tron compact EV starts at £32,200 (approximately $45,000) while delivering exceptional energy efficiency through a low drag coefficient. The vehicle offers multiple battery and drivetrain configuration options to optimize range and affordability. It addresses a rare combination in the EV market: both competitive pricing and superior efficiency.
content:
When shopping for an electric vehicle, affordability is becoming a more common trait. But affordable and energy efficient is truly a rare breed. Often you have to sacrifice one for the other. Want something affordable? Great, here's a range loser. Want something that goes the distance? Be ready to pay the price.  
Surprisingly, here comes Audi to split the difference. The German automaker's new A2 E-tron compact crossover is inexpensive, starting at just £32,200 (about $45,000). And it absolutely impresses with an ultra low drag coefficient and a range of battery and drivetrain options that, when configured correctly, can produce a range of …

content: The rise of AI has brought an avalanche of new terms and slang. Here is a glossary with definitions of some of the most important words and phrases you might encounter.

title: A secret new Elizabeth Holmes documentary stuns Telluride
summary: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim created a documentary titled 'You Can See Everything' about Elizabeth Holmes that premiered at the Telluride Film Festival. The film provides unprecedented access to the Theranos founder, offering new perspectives on her story. The surprise premiere generated significant attention among festival attendees.
content: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's secret Elizabeth Holmes documentary, "You Can See Everything," stunned Telluride audiences Sunday night with its generous access to the Theranos founder.

title: Six years later, Sony revisits its legendary XM4 headphones
summary: Sony has reintroduced its acclaimed WH-1000XM4 headphones as the WH-1000XM4C with minor improvements, bringing back the compact design from the original 2020 model that dominated best-of lists for years before going out of stock. The new version maintains the iconic design with added color options like lavender.
content:
The XM4C (in white) have the exact same visual design as the XM4 (in black) from 2020. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge	

Six years ago Sony and Bose were in the middle of a noise-canceling battle, with each new model of headphones better than the last. In the fall of 2020, Sony released the WH-1000XM4 headphones to wide acclaim. They sat atop best headphones lists for years, thanks to their great sound, competitive ANC, and compact size, until they went out of stock. Now Sony has brought them back, with minor improvements, as the WH-1000XM4C.
The XM4C look identical to the original XM4 (although they now have a lavender option), with the same hinge design and ability to fold up. It's a compact design that Sony moved away from when it released the XM5 in 2022, …

title: EcoFlow makes the miniature power station even smaller
summary: EcoFlow's new fourth-generation River series includes compact power stations with 256Wh and 512Wh capacities, offering 2.5x and 5x the energy of the largest airline-approved power banks respectively. The batteries use longer-lasting LFP chemistry and feature multiple USB and AC output options for powering various portable devices.
content:
The River 260 Gen4 (on the table) powering a portable fridge, Starlink Mini, and charging a phone. | Image: EcoFlow	

If you're in the market for a tiny power station that punches well above its size and weight then have a look at EcoFlow's new fourth-generation River series. 
The River 260 Gen4 features a 256Wh capacity battery while the 520 Gen4 packs in 512Wh - storing about 2.5x and 5x the energy of the largest airline-approved power banks, respectively. Better yet, the batteries are built using longer-lasting LFP chemistry that's far less volatile. The River 260 Gen4 features four USB ports, and 300W of max continuous output delivered out its lone AC jack. title: The real reason your phone is getting more expensive
summary: Apple's upcoming iPhone release is likely to feature a price increase driven by soaring memory chip costs, reflecting a reversal of decades of declining memory prices that once drove consumer electronics affordability. Industry discussion of memory shortages and pricing surged in company transcripts last quarter, signaling this cost inflation trend is widespread across manufacturers.
content:
When Apple debuts the next generation of iPhones this week, they're likely to come with an unwanted change: a higher price tag. A price hike from the supply-chain powerhouse would be the clearest sign yet that soaring memory costs have become unavoidable - with no end to the memory crunch in sight.
Call it "chipflation" or "RAMageddon." The shortage is reversing a decades-long decline in memory costs that helped make consumer electronics more powerful without making them dramatically more expensive. The terms "memory prices" and "memory shortage" appeared in 473 company transcripts last quarter, according to data provided by AlphaSense. The …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: 你的手机为什么越来越贵
zh.summary: 苹果即将推出的iPhone预计因内存芯片成本飙升而涨价，这反映了数十年内存价格下跌趋势的逆转。这种曾经推动消费电子产品平价化的价格下跌现已不再。上季度公司财报中内存短缺和定价讨论显著增加，表明这种成本通胀趋势在各制造商中普遍存在。

summary: Bentley is launching its 2027 Torcal electric SUV, a luxury vehicle that shares a platform with the Porsche Cayenne and competes with high-end EVs like the Rolls-Royce Spectre and Mercedes EQS. The Torcal aims to balance traditional automotive authenticity with modern electric technology. The vehicle will officially debut later this month following pre-launch test drives.
content:

Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac's Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne.

title: Huawei copies Samsung’s privacy display in its latest trifold
summary: Huawei has unveiled the Mate XT 2, its third trifold smartphone, adopting Samsung's inward-folding design and privacy-enhancing display technology similar to the Galaxy S26 Ultra. This marks a strategic shift from the first Mate XT's accordion-style folding, which exposed parts of the display. The move demonstrates Huawei's competitive positioning in the premium foldable phone segment.
content:
Huawei has released its third trifold phone in China, and the company has clearly had half an eye on Samsung during development. Not only does the Mate XT 2 adopt the inward-folding form factor used on Samsung's Galaxy Z TriFold, it's also the first foldable to include a privacy-enhancing display, much like the one Samsung added to the Galaxy S26 Ultra this year.
